claimsToVerify: Plague doctor beak mask dates primarily to the 17th century (invented by Charles Delorme circa 1619) rather than the 14th-century Black Death.
Municipalities hired dedicated plague doctors specifically to care for the poor, maintain civic order, record casualties, and inspect quarantined homes.
Wooden canes were used by plague doctors to examine patients or check pulses without direct skin contact.
